reasoning: PairPODKokkos::compute() (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:186-256) has no early return for inum==0.  At line 254-256: 'nAtomBlocks = calculateNumberOfIntervals(inum, atomBlockSize); if (nAtomBlocks > 100) nAtomBlocks = 100; divideInterval(atomBlocks, inum, nAtomBlocks);'.  calculateNumberOfIntervals (line 475-483) is 'int M = N / intervalSize; if (N % intervalSize != 0) M++; return M;' -- with N==0 and intervalSize==2048 (set in the ctor, line 61) it returns 0 and the remainder bump does not fire.  divideInterval (line 461-472) then does 'int intervalSize = N / M;' with M==0, i.e. 0/0 integer division -> SIGFPE on x86 / UB.  The CPU base is not affected: PairPOD::compute() hard-codes 'int blockMode = 0;' (src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:186) and only the blockMode==0 branch runs; the identical block code in the 'else if (blockMode == 1)' branch (pair_pod.cpp:236-239) is dead.  inum==0 is reachable on any rank whose subdomain holds no owned atoms.
fix: In PairPODKokkos<DeviceType>::compute(), after ev_init/per-atom array setup and after 'inum = list->inum;' is known, return early when inum == 0 (still doing the fdotr/virial bookkeeping that the normal exit path performs), or make calculateNumberOfIntervals() return MAX(1,M).

reasoning: blockatom_base_descriptors() (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:1385-1474) calls 'set_array_to_zero(d2, Ni*nl2);' before twobodydesc(), but the corresponding zeroing for the other slices is commented out: line 1436 '//set_array_to_zero(d3, Ni*nl3);' and line 1445 '//set_array_to_zero(d4, Ni*nl4);'.  The d33/d34/d44 slices never had one.  Each of those slices is only written inside a guarded block ('if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nij>1))', '(nl4>0) && (Nij>2)', '(nl33>0) && (Nij>3)', '(nl34>0) && (Nij>4)', '(nl44>0) && (Nij>5)'), and the kernels that fill them assign rather than accumulate (threebodydesc line 916 'd3(...) = tmp', fourbodydesc line 1079 'd4(i + Ni*kk) = tmp', crossdesc line 1355 'd12(n + Ni*i) = ...'), so when a guard is false nothing writes the slice.  bd is a persistent member view (declared src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.h:147, allocated once in grow_atoms(), src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:496) reused for every atom block and every timestep, so the previous block's/step's values survive and are consumed by blockatom_base_coefficients() (line 1477-1499), which sums cefs[1+m+nc]*B[n+Ni*m] over all Mdesc entries.  The CPU reference does zero everything: EAPOD::peratombase_descriptors (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:806) 'for (int i=0; i<Mdesc; i++) bd1[i] = 0.0;' followed by 'if (Nj == 0) return;'.  So the KOKKOS result is history-dependent whenever a block's pair count falls at or below one of the thresholds after having been above it.
fix: Zero the whole descriptor block once at the top of blockatom_base_descriptors(): replace 'set_array_to_zero(d2, Ni*nl2);' with 'set_array_to_zero(bd, Ni*Mdesc);' (or re-enable the commented-out per-slice set_array_to_zero calls and add ones for d33/d34/d44) before the guarded blocks.

reasoning: The mechanism is exactly as described: PairPODKokkos::neighflag is a plain 'int neighflag;' member (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.h:50) that the constructor (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:47-67) never initializes, and init_style() (line 87-108) assigns it only after the host branch: 'if (host_flag) { ...; PairPOD::init_style(); return; }' at lines 89-95, with 'neighflag = lmp->kokkos->neighflag;' at line 101.  compute() then reads it at line 192: 'if (neighflag == FULL) no_virial_fdotr_compute = 1;'.  So every host-space (CPU-only Kokkos) run reads an indeterminate value -- real undefined behaviour, and a MSan/valgrind hit.  I downgrade the severity, though: the two outcomes are numerically equivalent.  Pair::ev_setup (src/pair.cpp:975-978) makes vflag_global and vflag_fdotr mutually exclusive, so garbage==FULL (1) merely routes the global virial through tallystress() (line 1716-1750, which sums -rij*fij) instead of through pair_virial_fdotr_compute() (line 310); both give the same pair virial with newton on, which the style requires.  No wrong-answer path was found, so this is a latent UB/hygiene defect, not a medium-severity correctness bug.
fix: Initialize 'neighflag = HALF;' (or FULL, matching the non-host path's expectation) in the PairPODKokkos constructor next to the other member initializations at src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:56-64, and/or move 'neighflag = lmp->kokkos->neighflag;' above the 'if (host_flag) { ... return; }' block in init_style().

reasoning: In the KOKKOS style the guards are on Nij, the number of (i,j) pairs in the ENTIRE atom block: compute() sets 'nij = NeighborCount(numij, rcutsq, gi1, ni);' (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:272) for a block of up to atomBlockSize=2048 atoms and passes it down through blockatom_energyforce(ei, fij, ni, nij) into blockatom_base_descriptors(bd, Ni, Nij), where the tests read 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nij>1))' (line 1421), '(nl4 > 0) && (Nij>2)' (line 1443), '(nl33>0) && (Nij>3)' (line 1452), '(nl34>0) && (Nij>4)' (line 1460), '(nl44>0) && (Nij>5)' (line 1468); blockatom_energyforce() repeats the same Nij tests for crossdesc_reduction and the force coefficients (lines 1641-1668).  The reference EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1195-1320) applies the identical thresholds to Nj, the neighbor count of the ONE atom being processed: 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nj>1))', '(nl23>0) && (Nj>2)', '(nl33>0) && (Nj>3)', '(nl4 > 0) && (Nj>2)', '(nl34>0) && (Nj>4)', '(nl44>0) && (Nj>5)', and this is the routine PairPOD::compute() actually calls (src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:214).  Consequence: for an atom with <=5 neighbors sitting in a block that has many pairs overall, KOKKOS evaluates three-/four-body and cross descriptors that the CPU sets to zero (bd1 is zeroed first, eapod.cpp:1207), and those descriptors are not zero for small Nj (e.g. d33 = d3*d3 from a single-neighbor sumU).  Energies and forces for undercoordinated atoms (dimers, gas-phase monomers, adatoms, small clusters) therefore differ between pod and pod/kk.  Conversely, the KOKKOS guard can also switch off the terms for a whole block that happens to have few pairs.  Forces use the same Nij guards, so the KOKKOS result is at least self-consistent, but it does not reproduce the CPU model.
fix: Make the guards per-atom rather than per-block: the block already has the per-atom pair counts in numij (numij(i+1)-numij(i) is atom i's neighbor count).  Either pass that count into the kernels and mask each atom's contribution (write zeros for atoms below the threshold), or drop the Nij thresholds and instead zero the whole bd/cb block (see F0383) and multiply each atom's three-/four-body/cross terms by a per-atom mask derived from numij.
